01THE CONNECTION

What LiveKit does

LiveKit provides a real-time room for audio and video. The Agents framework lets our Python program join that room and coordinate an AI conversation.

A LIVEKIT ROOM
ParticipantMicrophone
Camera
Speaker
⇄
Python agentGemini
Instructions
Tool functions

Media tracks connect the two participants.

Why it helps here
We use room connections and media handling instead of building all the streaming infrastructure ourselves.
Where people use it
Voice assistants, tutoring apps, customer support calls, and interactive audio or video experiences.
What Cloud adds
Our LiveKit Cloud project provides managed infrastructure. The Python agent can run locally during development.

01THE CONNECTION

Two services, two sets of credentials

LiveKit credentials connect the room. GOOGLE_API_KEY lets the Google plugin authenticate to Gemini.

LiveKit Cloud
Create or choose a project, then authenticate with the CLI.
Google AI Studio
Create a Gemini API key and add it locally. The plugin reads GOOGLE_API_KEY from the environment.
Costs and secrets
A key does not guarantee free usage. Check model availability and limits. Keep .env.local out of Git and off the shared screen.

01THE CONNECTION

Our first voice conversation

Open the console link, start a session, allow the microphone, and speak. This agent waits for the participant to start.

SAY THIS FIRST
“Syrus, you there?”
EXACT RULE IN OUR PROMPT

“Right here. What’s the situation?”

What this proves
The room connection, microphone input, Gemini call, and spoken output work together.
A follow-up
Ask for a short workshop introduction. Then ask for a shorter version to test a second turn.
If it stays quiet
Check the worker is running, the console agent selection, microphone permission, and terminal errors. A transcript may arrive after the audio.

02THE CHARACTER

Why we use Gemini Live

Our project uses a realtime model that handles speech input and spoken output. It also supports the camera questions we want to demonstrate.

The model name
This string chooses the Gemini model. It is set in our code, rather than inferred from the agent’s name.
The current voice
Aoede selects the sound of the generated speech.
Another architecture
A modular pipeline uses separate speech-to-text, language model, and text-to-speech providers. It offers more component choices but more configuration.
NEXT IN THE STORYThe model gives Syrus capabilities. The instructions give those capabilities a character.
Model configuration ↗Google Live API capabilities ↗
02THE CHARACTER

The system prompt is Syrus’s brief

A system prompt gives the agent standing instructions about its role, response style, tools, and boundaries.

OUR PROMPT STRUCTURE
  1. PersonaWho Syrus is and how it sounds in conversation
  2. Output rulesShort plain-spoken replies, one question at a time
  3. Conversational flowUseful steps, clear results, honest failures
  4. Hard rule + exampleA specific response and a sample tone
  5. Tools + guardrailsWhen to fetch data and what to avoid
CURRENT OPENING
“You are Syrus, a helpful AI with the persona of a witty confidante.”

“Syrus” comes from these instructions. The LiveKit dispatch name my-agent identifies the worker separately.

NEXT IN THE STORYWe can rewrite the role while keeping the tool rules and boundaries consistent.

02THE CHARACTER

Personality and voice are separate

The prompt shapes what Syrus says. The voice setting selects how its speech sounds.

Our comparison
Keep the same prompt and ask the same question. Listen for the delivery that suits your audience.
Choosing a voice
Use the provider’s supported voice names and samples. Persona wording does not select an audio voice.
Fish Audio as an extension
Fish Audio uses a separate TTS integration. Its voice IDs do not replace Gemini voice names directly. Separate TTS needs additional configuration.

03THE CONTEXT

Our co-host needs visual context

Suppose the workshop agenda is on a page. Instead of describing every line, we can show it to Syrus through the camera.

What changes
video_input=True enables video input for the session. Microphone audio remains enabled.
What you do
Allow camera access in the console, show a clear object or page, and ask a specific question.
How it works here
Gemini interprets supplied camera frames. Vision is built-in input rather than a function in AssistantTools.

03THE CONTEXT

The camera experiment

We will check both a clear view and a missing view. A good answer should follow the evidence currently available.

01

A clear object

Hold up a mug.

“What am I holding? Describe the visible details.”
02

A useful page

Show the workshop agenda.

“Read the heading and suggest a shorter title.”
03

An uncertain view

Move the object out of view.

“Can you still see it clearly right now?”
What we are testing

Object description, readable text, and honesty about what the current view supports. Prior frames may remain in the conversation context.

NEXT IN THE STORYSeeing the agenda helps. But the camera cannot tell us today’s weather or the latest documentation.
03THE CONTEXT

Why we need live data

Syrus can explain what rain is from general knowledge. A question about today’s weather needs information tied to a place and time.

GENERAL KNOWLEDGE

“How does rain form?”

The model can explain a concept using learned patterns and the conversation.

That explanation does not establish current conditions outside.

LIVE DATA

“Will it rain in Bengaluru today?”

A tool fetches current conditions and today’s forecast from an external service.

The agent still needs to check the location, source, and relevance.

Live dataInformation retrieved from an external source at the time of the request.
NEXT IN THE STORYTools give our agent a defined way to request that outside information.
03THE CONTEXT

The tools Syrus has today

A tool is a function the model can request with arguments. Python performs the request and returns data the model can use.

ToolWhen it helpsWhere data comes from
search_the_web

Research, explicit searches, and current information

DDGS search results
get_weather

Current conditions and today’s forecast for a city

Open-Meteo API
define_word

English meanings and available pronunciation data

Free Dictionary API

Search may help with many questions. Dedicated tools give predictable fields for a specific job. Our camera input sits outside this callable tool list.

03THE CONTEXT

Inside the web search function

The decorator exposes a callable function. Its description and query argument help the model understand when and how to use it.

The query
A concise string, such as “LiveKit Agents voice AI quickstart”.
The async boundary
DDGS search is synchronous here. to_thread keeps that work off the event loop.
The real implementation
It trims empty queries, handles search failures, and reports no results. The excerpt omits those checks.
NEXT IN THE STORYA Python function alone is not enough. The assistant must receive it as an available tool.
Complete search function ↗DDGS backend behavior ↗
03THE CONTEXT

How Syrus gets access to a tool

The function must exist, appear in the registered tool list, and have clear guidance in the system prompt.

SYSTEM PROMPT GUIDANCE
“Use web search for general research and current information.”
Registration
Makes the function available to the model.
Instructions
Explain when it is appropriate. The model still decides whether to request it.
Tool result
The function returns data. Syrus turns it into a concise spoken explanation.

03THE CONTEXT

One weather request, end to end

The user asks a question. Gemini decides to request a function, and Python supplies the evidence for the final reply.

  1. 01

    You ask

    “What is the weather in Bengaluru, India, today?”

  2. 02

    Gemini requests a tool

    get_weather(location="Bengaluru, India")

  3. 03

    Python fetches data

    Resolve the city, request Open-Meteo data, and validate the response.

  4. 04

    Syrus answers

    Summarize the returned conditions and forecast in ordinary speech.

Illustrative call shape. The actual location argument can differ. Missing or ambiguous locations should lead to clarification.

NEXT IN THE STORYNow we can verify the tool activity instead of trusting the sound of the answer.
Weather implementation ↗
03THE CONTEXT

The live tool check

The console’s tool activity gives us a second view of what happened. A fluent answer alone does not prove a tool ran.

Search

“Search the web for the latest LiveKit Agents documentation and give me the relevant link.”

Look for search_the_web and a relevant query.
Weather

“What is the weather in Bengaluru, India, today?”

Look for get_weather with a specific location.
Definition

“What does serendipity mean?”

Look for define_word with the requested word.
A useful failure check

Ask “What is the weather?” Syrus should request a location. If a service fails, it should explain the failure rather than invent data.

04YOUR NEXT CHAPTER

A useful agent needs honest limits

Good behavior includes asking for missing information, describing uncertainty, and keeping private data out of the conversation.

Brief and accessible
Small steps, one question at a time, and simple spoken answers.
Respectful by default
Use the person’s stated name and pronouns. Keep humor away from identity or distress.
Evidence before claims
Do not claim to open a page, buy something, or see a hidden object.
BOUNDARY TEST
“Open that website and buy the ticket for me.”

Syrus can search for information, but this project has no browser actions or purchasing tool.

External search results are reference data. Their embedded instructions should not override the agent’s own rules.

NEXT IN THE STORYThe next feature should strengthen a real use case while keeping those boundaries clear.

Your next experiment

Choose one feature that solves a specific problem. Explain its input, its result, and what happens when it fails.

START SMALL

A focused API tool

Add a time-zone or public events lookup. Define the function, register it, and describe when Syrus should call it.

Success check The result answers a real request.
Failure check Missing input or an unavailable service produces a clear response.

GO FURTHER

An MCP connection

Model Context Protocol lets an agent connect to a compatible server that exposes tools.

Choose a trusted server and a small set of permissions. MCP is an optional extension, not part of this project today.

04YOUR NEXT CHAPTER

A short glossary

The names you saw in the code, in ordinary language.

Agent
A program that uses a model and tools to help with a task.
LiveKit room
A shared session containing participants and media tracks.
Realtime model
A model that processes streaming input for an interactive conversation.
System prompt
Standing instructions that guide the agent’s behavior.
API
A defined interface for requesting data or actions from software.
Tool calling
The model requests a registered function with arguments.
STT / TTS
Speech-to-text turns audio into text. Text-to-speech produces audio from text.
MCP
Model Context Protocol, a standard for connecting compatible tool servers and clients.
